newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle markets quiet - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle markets quiet - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet late Thursday, with a few sales reported at $62.00 to $63.00 per cwt, feedlot sources said.
Sources said enough cattle were sold this week to keep lots current, but the sale prices were disappointing. Most sources said the $63.00 prices did not cover production costs.
Many of this week's sales have been delivered to packers or were scheduled for shipment Friday.
"We are going to ship everything we did tomorrow (Friday) morning," a Oklahoma feedlot manager said.
A Kansas manager said about half his sales have been shipped and another said a good portion of this week's sales were loaded out early Thursday.

The recent downtrend in cash beef prices has pressured cattle prices as well taking bids from $64.00 at the beginning of June in the central and southern Plains, to $63.00 now. In that time beef prices have trended lower, with USDA quoting 700- to 850-lb choice carcasses at $98.24 per cwt at midday Thursday, down from $103.51 on June 2.
